name: Joha
overview: Joha was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified primarily as the son of Beriah. His mention in Scripture is brief and specific, focusing on his genealogical placement within the tribe. There are no additional notes or details about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Joha appears only once in Scripture, in 1 Chronicles 8:16, without a provided meaning or divine attribution. Therefore, the name is simply recognized as a proper name without further significance indicated in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Joha is explicitly recorded as the son of Beriah, establishing his direct familial link within the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further information about his family or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Joha's significance lies in his genealogical mention, which contributes to the biblical record of the tribe of Benjamin's lineage. Such genealogies serve to preserve the heritage and identity of God's people, underscoring the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant through successive generations. Although no narrative actions are ascribed to Joha, his inclusion affirms the importance of every member within the covenant community.
